title: Go: Mutex and Synchronization
description: Protect shared state with sync.Mutex and avoid race conditions in concurrent Go programs.

steps.title: Protect a counter with mutex
steps.description: Create a `Counter` struct with a `sync.Mutex`. Launch 10 goroutines each incrementing the counter 1000 times. Print the final value (should be 10000).
hints: Embed `sync.Mutex` in the struct or use it as a field

verification.successMessage: Mutex protected the counter — no race condition!
verification.failureMessage: Make sure you call Lock before incrementing and Unlock after.

steps.title: Lock/Unlock pattern
steps.description: Implement a thread-safe `Set(key string, val int)` and `Get(key string) int` method on a `SafeMap` struct using a mutex. Print a fetched value.
hints: Use a `map[string]int` as the underlying storage
Use defer to ensure Unlock happens even on panic

verification.failureMessage: Both Get and Set must lock the mutex.

steps.title: RWMutex read vs write
steps.description: Use `sync.RWMutex` for a shared config map. Write locks use `Lock()/Unlock()`, read locks use `RLock()/RUnlock()`. Print the config value.
hints: `Lock` blocks all readers and writers — exclusive access
Use RLock for getters, Lock for setters

verification.successMessage: RWMutex allows concurrent reads with exclusive writes!
verification.failureMessage: Make sure you use RLock for read operations and Lock for writes.

steps.title: Deadlock avoidance
steps.description: Create a scenario with two mutexes (`muA`, `muB`) and two goroutines that lock them in the same order. If they lock in opposite order, deadlock occurs. Implement correct ordering and print "done".
hints: Always acquire multiple locks in the same order across goroutines
Lock muA then muB in both goroutines to avoid deadlock
A deadlock causes Go's runtime to crash with 'fatal error: all goroutines are asleep'

verification.failureMessage: Ensure both goroutines lock muA before muB.

steps.title: sync.Once
steps.description: Use `sync.Once` to ensure an initialization function (printing "Initialized") runs exactly once even when called from multiple goroutines. Launch 5 goroutines calling the init function.
hints: The function passed to Do runs only once, no matter how many times Do is called

verification.failureMessage: Use once.Do() to wrap your initialization function.
